methods.completeness: Independently reconstruct all 104 timber envelopes from saved prejoinery halfspaces. Prove every envelope cell lies in final timber wood or exported cavity, conserve partition volume, and check every cavity vertex lies inside its original envelope. The 16 declared exterior two-inch brace stop trims are applied explicitly. This detects unexported overcuts, omitted cavities and undersized cavity diagnostics.
methods.containment: Positive-volume cavity components are partitioned into disjoint convex cells when concave or shared by multiple mates. Every cell is proved inside its actual source cavity; volume conservation rejects missing cells. Winding-confirmed mate interior points and clipped boundary triangles prove mating coverage, excluding the explicit 1e-8 m tolerance shell.
methods.hull_conditioning: Convex verification cells use physical halfspaces and volume directly, avoiding numerical winding artifacts from artificial hull triangulations. Qhull uses deterministic centered, axis-scaled and principal-axis affine fallback frames with default/exact-merge options. Exported source surfaces still require raw topology, winding and signed-volume validation; nonconvex source partitions must recover their original signed volume. No random jitter, vertex perturbation, discarded cells or enlarged fit tolerances are used.
methods.legacy_residuals: Legacy 3D unfilled Boolean meshes may have negative volumes and rotation-dependent artifacts. They are diagnostics, not evidence of physical gaps.
methods.raw_surfaces: Project original mesh triangles to common planes and use scaled 2D polygon intersections. Positive-area coincident patches fail whether normals are opposed or same-facing; edge/point contact is permitted. This detects surface folds and duplicate patches that signed-volume/solid-occupancy checks can cancel.
methods.sampling: Independent solid-angle winding numbers for deterministic scrambled Sobol points and inward-offset triangle centroids.
methods.sections: Canonical bay coordinates; scaled Clipper2 2D differences/intersections on three axes, just above/below vertex events and at interval quartiles. Exact coplanar boundary planes are excluded.
